Your hair is similar enough to mine that I'll share my tips that took a long time of trial and error and a very lucky find of a master barber who gave me custom advice.

0. When you get a cut you are focusing on how it grows in, not just how it looks at the time.

1. Avoid thinning shears like the plague. Blending the line between your sides and top is generally OK. Never on the top.

2. Clippers on the sides are OK. On the top is only acceptable if they scissor cut afterward.

3. You need a point cut. That is when you cut "into" the hair or at a diagonal to facilitate curls and remove bulk without thinning shears. If they don't know how to point cut, don't let them cut.

4. Parts and bangs are still mostly at the expertise of the stylist or barber. Ask them for advice on what is natural for your growth patterns and work with it.

5. Trends are not something you can follow quite as much. The good news is curls always look good.

6. Specialized curly cuts are growing in popularity but require a specialist and you probably need to grow out your curls more. Online communities focused on curly hair will know more.

7. You may have to dig around for a good stylist. Don't hesitate to explore options until you find a good one. Barbers, specialized barbers, upscale salons, budget salons, and alternative salons are all fair game.

8. Don't just trust stylists who say they specialize in curly hair. Ask about point cuts and thinning shears first and be insistent.

9. For styling, you seem to have a more naturally bouncy curl than I do, so you might get away with no product. I use a specific brand to style. Creams, pomades, and gels can all work depending on how wet you want the look, or you can get away with a more natural approach. Try out everything.
